findings.description: When Step 11.5's `new|changed` branch runs `git add` successfully and then `git commit` fails (hook, signing, etc.), the handler only sets `SKIP_REASON="git commit failed"` and returns. The ledger pair stays staged (`A` for a first audit, `M` for a re-audit) while the step prints `audit-choices: skipped (git commit failed) — continuing to summary`. That contradicts the step's own decline-to-commit cleanup used on the early SKIP_REASON and partial-pair paths, which restore or `rm -f` per path so the worktree is left clean. Reproduced: with a failing `commit-msg` hook, status remains `A  openspec/changes/.../choices.json` / `choices.md` after the skip; `git checkout --` alone does not clear an index-only `A` add. A later unrelated `git commit` can therefore land the ledger after the step claimed it skipped. `test_git_commit_failure_sets_skip_reason_not_silent` only covers the byte-identical-to-HEAD "nothing to commit" shape (clean index), so it stays green while this staged-orphan failure mode is unpinned.
findings.resolution: On `git commit` failure, unstage the two ledger paths (`git reset HEAD -- "$JSON_PATH" "$MD_PATH"`) and then run the same per-path tracked/`git checkout --` vs untracked/`rm -f` discard used elsewhere before returning. Extend the executable commit-failure test to stage real content changes under a failing hook and assert `git status --porcelain` is empty afterward while still expecting `SKIP_REASON=git commit failed`.
